subject: Post-demo: air-gapped upgrade path + firmware compatibility
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@biogen.com>, ops+infra@biogen.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 15:12:00 -0500
Subject: Post-demo recap: air-gapped deployment needs and next steps

Hi Alex / Biogen infra team,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciated the thoughtful questions about upgrade windows and offline ops. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can prepare the right artifacts: 

- Deployment mode: primary interest is Private (air-gapped) appliance inside your US data centers; you also asked about fallback to Dedicated during scheduled maintenance.
- Hardware confirmation needed: model/sku of servers + GPU firmware levels (we've noted you mentioned 4x A100-per-node in the call).
- Upgrade cadence: you asked how we handle zero-network upgrades for minor patches vs. full model/firmware updates (we described two options: maintenance media + signed package, or on-site USB with attestations).
- Offline observability: you asked about log shipping and pulling traces post-upgrade — we said we can export audit bundles and support on-site collection scripts.

Next steps we recommend:
1) Please share a short inventory stub (hostname, server model, current firmware & OS) for one representative rack.
2) Confirm which upgrade model you prefer for a proof-of-concept (POC): "signed-media" (we prepare signed update tarball you load via airgap media) or "on-site-assisted" (Redwood engineer brings media + runs MOP on-site).
3) We will produce a lightweight airgap upgrade checklist and a firmware compatibility matrix for your hardware.

I'll follow up with the checklist and a draft MOP. Could we target next Wed 21 Jan for a 30-min POC scoping call?

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-airgap-checklist-v1.2.pdf (stub), firmware-compat-table.xlsx (stub)

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@biogen.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 09:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: air-gapped deployment needs and next steps

Thanks Grace — good summary. A few clarifications from our infra side:

- Inventory: I'll export a minimal CSV for the sample rack and send by EOD Friday. It will include server model, BIOS/firmware, GPU driver and OS build.
- Firmware: we are on NVIDIA driver 470.x and BIOS 2.3.1 for that rack. We do periodic firmware maintenance on a quarterly schedule.
- Upgrade preference: leaning toward signed-media for the POC to keep vendor presence minimal, but we may want on-site-assisted for the full rollout.

Question: for signed-media, do you support an HSM/KMS verification step we can run locally to validate the package prior to applying? We need to present that to security.

Alex
Alex Chen, Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Biogen | Platform Infra

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@biogen.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 11:42:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: air-gapped deployment needs and next steps

Alex — thanks for the details. Short technical answers: 

- HSM/KMS check: yes. For signed-media we ship a signed tarball and a separate signature file. Customers can verify using either a supplied Redwood public key (RSA-4096) or through their own HSM verifying the signature via pkcs#7. We will provide verification scripts you can run offline.

- Firmware compatibility: the compatibility matrix attached lists tested driver/BIOS/OS combos. For NVIDIA 470.x + BIOS 2.3.1 we mark 'compatible with caveats' — specifically we require kernel patch KB-2025 to avoid a timeout condition under continuous batching. If you can't patch kernel, we can recommend a small config change (reduce persistent worker count) as a workaround for POC.

- Offline upgrade MOP: we support two MOPs: (1) signed-media automated path (fully offline, limited operator steps), and (2) on-site-assisted where our engineer runs the sequence and produces an audit bundle. Both produce the same end-state; on-site-assisted is slower but less operational risk for first rollout.

I'll drop a short MOP outline and a verification script in the drive link Grace referenced.

- Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: ops+infra@biogen.com
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 08:27:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: air-gapped deployment needs and next steps

Rishi / Grace — quick follow-up from the infra team after reviewing the compatibility matrix you sent: 

- KB-2025 kernel patch: we cannot apply kernel patches outside our quarterly window for production racks, however we can apply a kernel param change for the POC rack. Can you confirm the exact sysctl we should change and the expected performance impact?
- For signed-media verification: we run Vault HSM-backed PKI and would like to import the Redwood public cert into our CA trust store. Please provide the cert and the exact import/getpubkey steps.

Also, if we go with signed-media for the POC, will the rollback steps be offline-only as well? Need to confirm we can recover without connecting to Redwood.

Thanks,
Biogen Infra Ops

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@biogen.com>, ops+infra@biogen.com
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jan 2026 09:30:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: air-gapped deployment needs and next steps

Alex / Team — thanks for the questions. Short answers and next steps to keep momentum: 

- Sysctl change for POC: set net.core.somaxconn=4096 and add the kernel parameter 'rd.batch_timeout_ms=250' in your boot conf for the POC rack only. Expected perf impact: <5% latency increase at 95th percentile in our internal tests for small bursts; we will validate against your trace during the POC.

- Public cert + import steps: Rishi, attached is the Redwood verification cert (PEM) and an import snippet for Vault PKI we recommend. I'll put the exact script in the Drive link.

- Rollback: signed-media rollback is fully offline — we provide a signed rollback tarball and a one-step restore script that runs locally and validates checksums. No network connection to Redwood is required for rollback.

Action items and owners:
- Biogen: send sample inventory CSV (Alex) — target: Fri 16 Jan (you indicated EOD Fri; if delayed, please let us know).
- Redwood: upload signed-media package example, verification script, and MOP v0.1 to Drive (Rishi) — target: Tue 20 Jan.
- Schedule POC scoping call: Wed 21 Jan, 11:00 AM EST (Grace to send invite).

I'll attach the MOP v0.1 and the firmware compatibility table here. If that timing looks good I'll lock the calendar invite.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-airgap-checklist-v1.2.pdf, firmware-compat-table.xlsx
